story_type: crippled spacecraft comes home: parachutes, splashdown, swimmers and helicopter pickup, historic TV
hook: Their oxygen tank blew up 200,000 miles from Earth.
narration: Their oxygen tank blew up two hundred thousand miles from Earth.
This was Apollo 13 in April 1970, three men on their way to the Moon.
Oxygen tank number two exploded, and tank number one failed with it.
Flight controllers turned the lunar module into a lifeboat for the long trip home.
Four days later, the capsule fell back through the atmosphere at more than five g's.
Then the main parachutes opened over the Pacific, and the crowds watching erupted.
It came down about four miles from the recovery ship, USS Iwo Jima.
Swimmers wrapped a flotation collar around it and dropped rafts with sea anchors, so the helicopter's downwash could not flip them.
Then a Navy helicopter lifted the astronauts out of the ocean one by one.
outcome: The helicopter landed on the Iwo Jima, and all three Apollo 13 astronauts walked out onto the deck.
title: Apollo 13 made it home
question_comment: Would you have trusted the lunar module to get you home?

description:
Apollo 13 splashes down in the Pacific near Samoa on April 17, 1970, four days after an oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon, and a Navy helicopter brings the crew to USS Iwo Jima.
